alignments.note: Auxiliary rides with the participle under rules 7 and 9; head on the lexical verb.
Inflected verb takes its English subject and lexical verb under rule 9.
The English preposition governing the phrase realizes the Greek preposition under rule 36.
Ordinary negative, not interrogative; rule 44 does not apply.

The participle carries the concessive force, so the supplied *though* is its rule 7 helper, discontinuously under rule 15; the supplied object *him* stays with the verb that requires it under rule 74. Attaching *though* to the adverb remains defensible, the source gloss reading it there.
The adversative conjunction is realized by *yet*; reading *yet* as a supplied correlative of *though* on the participle is defensible.
One Greek verb rendered *rejoice greatly*, with its English subject under rule 9; head on the lexical verb.
No article stands to anchor a determiner, so the case preposition rides with the noun under rules 21 and 23.
One Greek participle rendered by an adjectival phrase; *glory* glosses the lexeme, so rule 66 heads there rather than on the completing *full*.
